subject: Cloud Computing
prompt: Which cloud service model gives the customer virtual machines, storage and networks to manage?
explanation: IaaS exposes compute, storage and networking; the customer manages the operating system upward.

subject: Cloud Computing
prompt: Which cloud service model delivers a complete application that users simply log in to?
explanation: With SaaS the provider runs the whole application stack.

subject: Cloud Computing
prompt: What is an AWS Region made up of?
option_c: A group of edge locations only
explanation: A Region contains several physically separate Availability Zones.

subject: Cloud Computing
prompt: Which AWS service is designed for object storage?
explanation: S3 stores objects in buckets; EBS is block storage and EFS is file storage.

subject: Cloud Computing
prompt: Which AWS service distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets?
explanation: Elastic Load Balancing spreads requests across healthy targets.

subject: Cloud Computing
prompt: What does horizontal scaling mean?
option_a: Moving to a larger instance type
option_b: Adding more memory to one server
option_c: Increasing the disk size of one server
option_d: Adding more instances to share the load
explanation: Horizontal scaling changes the number of instances; vertical scaling changes their size.

subject: Cloud Computing
prompt: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, who patches the guest operating system on an EC2 instance?
explanation: AWS secures the underlying infrastructure; the customer manages the guest OS on EC2.

subject: Cloud Computing
prompt: Which AWS service creates infrastructure from declarative templates?
explanation: CloudFormation provisions stacks of resources from templates.

subject: Cloud Computing
prompt: Which AWS service collects metrics and triggers alarms?
explanation: CloudWatch stores metrics and logs and evaluates alarms.

subject: Cloud Computing
prompt: About how much downtime does 99.9% availability allow in a 30-day month?
explanation: 0.1% of 43,200 minutes is 43.2 minutes.

subject: Cloud Computing
prompt: Two components are both required and each has 99.9% availability. What is the approximate combined availability?
explanation: Serial availability multiplies: 0.999 x 0.999 is about 0.998.

subject: Cloud Computing
prompt: What is the main security benefit of attaching an IAM role to an EC2 instance?
option_a: The instance no longer needs a security group
option_b: Applications get temporary credentials without storing access keys
option_d: The instance can never be reached from the internet
explanation: The role supplies automatically rotated temporary credentials through instance metadata.

subject: Data Structures
prompt: Which order does a stack follow?
explanation: The most recently pushed item is popped first.

subject: Data Structures
prompt: Which order does a queue follow?
explanation: Items leave a queue in the order they arrived.

subject: Data Structures
prompt: Which data structure is normally used for breadth-first search?
explanation: A queue visits nodes level by level.

subject: Data Structures
prompt: What is the worst-case time of binary search on a sorted array of n items?
explanation: Each comparison halves the remaining range.

subject: Data Structures
prompt: What is the average lookup time in a hash table with a good hash function?
explanation: Keys spread evenly, so buckets stay short on average.

subject: Data Structures
prompt: What does an inorder traversal of a binary search tree produce?
explanation: Left, node, right visits BST keys in sorted order.

subject: Data Structures
prompt: What is the worst-case time of quicksort?
explanation: Consistently poor pivots produce very unbalanced partitions.

subject: Data Structures
prompt: What is the worst-case time of merge sort?
explanation: There are log n levels of merging and each costs O(n).

subject: Data Structures
prompt: What is the time to insert at the head of a singly linked list?
explanation: Only the head pointer and one next pointer change.

subject: Data Structures
prompt: When can Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm give wrong answers?
option_a: When the graph has negative edge weights
explanation: Dijkstra assumes a settled distance can never be improved later.

subject: Data Structures
prompt: What is the time to build a binary heap from n items using bottom-up heapify?
explanation: Most nodes are near the leaves and sift down only a short distance.

subject: Data Structures
prompt: What is the height of an AVL tree containing n nodes?
explanation: AVL rotations keep the tree height balanced.

subject: Operating Systems
prompt: What do threads of the same process share?
explanation: Threads share code, data and heap, but each has its own stack and registers.

subject: Operating Systems
prompt: Which CPU scheduling algorithm uses a fixed time quantum?
explanation: Round robin gives each ready process a time slice in turn.

subject: Operating Systems
prompt: What does virtual memory allow?
option_a: The CPU to run without a cache
option_b: Disks to run faster than RAM
option_c: Programs to run without an operating system
option_d: A process to use an address space larger than physical memory
explanation: Pages can be kept on disk and loaded when needed.

subject: Operating Systems
prompt: Which of these is NOT a necessary condition for deadlock?
explanation: The necessary condition is no preemption.

subject: Operating Systems
prompt: What is thrashing?
option_b: The system spends more time paging than executing
option_d: A process creates too many threads
explanation: Too little memory causes constant page faults.

subject: Operating Systems
prompt: What is a semaphore used for?
explanation: Wait and signal operations coordinate processes or threads.

subject: Operating Systems
prompt: Which page replacement algorithm can show Belady's anomaly?
explanation: With FIFO, more frames can sometimes cause more page faults.

subject: Operating Systems
prompt: What is the Banker's algorithm used for?
explanation: It grants a request only if the system stays in a safe state.

subject: Operating Systems
prompt: For processes that arrive together, which algorithm gives the lowest average waiting time?
explanation: Running short jobs first reduces the wait of all the others.

subject: Operating Systems
prompt: What happens during a context switch?
option_b: The CPU state of one process is saved and another is loaded
option_c: A file is moved to disk
explanation: Registers and scheduling state are saved and restored.

subject: Operating Systems
prompt: Fixed-size allocation units mainly cause which problem?
explanation: Unused space remains inside the last allocated unit.

subject: Operating Systems
prompt: What does the translation lookaside buffer cache?
explanation: The TLB avoids walking the page table for every memory access.

subject: DBMS
prompt: What must a primary key do?
option_d: Uniquely identify each row and not be NULL
explanation: A primary key is unique and non-null.

subject: DBMS
prompt: Which SQL statement retrieves rows from a table?
explanation: SELECT reads data.

subject: DBMS
prompt: What does the A in ACID stand for?
explanation: A transaction happens completely or not at all.

subject: DBMS
prompt: Second normal form removes which kind of dependency?
option_b: Partial dependency on part of a composite key
explanation: Non-key attributes must depend on the whole key.

subject: DBMS
prompt: Third normal form removes which kind of dependency?
explanation: Non-key attributes must not depend on other non-key attributes.

subject: DBMS
prompt: What does a foreign key enforce?
explanation: Referenced rows must exist in the parent table.

subject: DBMS
prompt: What does an INNER JOIN return?
option_a: All rows from the left table
option_d: Only rows with matching values in both tables
explanation: Unmatched rows are excluded.

subject: DBMS
prompt: What is the usual trade-off of adding an index?
option_c: Faster reads but slower writes and more storage
explanation: Each write must also maintain the index.

subject: DBMS
prompt: Which clause filters groups after aggregation?
explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups.

subject: DBMS
prompt: What does strict adherence to two-phase locking guarantee?
explanation: 2PL ensures serializability but can still deadlock.

subject: DBMS
prompt: Which SQL-standard isolation level prevents phantom reads?
explanation: The standard allows phantoms at every lower level.

subject: DBMS
prompt: What is the rule of write-ahead logging?
option_a: Data pages are written before the log
option_b: Log records reach stable storage before the changed data pages
option_c: Logs are written only at shutdown
explanation: The log makes undo and redo possible after a crash.

subject: Computer Networks
prompt: What is the default port for HTTPS?
explanation: HTTPS uses TCP port 443 by default.

subject: Computer Networks
prompt: What does DNS do?
option_c: Translates domain names into IP addresses
explanation: DNS resolves names to records such as IP addresses.

subject: Computer Networks
prompt: What does DHCP provide to a host?
option_a: An IP address and network settings
explanation: DHCP leases addresses and configuration automatically.

subject: Computer Networks
prompt: Which statement about TCP is correct?
option_b: It is connection-oriented and provides reliable delivery
option_d: It works only on local networks
explanation: TCP uses handshakes, acknowledgements and retransmission.

subject: Computer Networks
prompt: At which OSI layer does IP routing take place?
explanation: Routers forward packets at layer 3.

subject: Computer Networks
prompt: How many usable host addresses does an IPv4 /24 subnet have?
explanation: The network and broadcast addresses are excluded from 256.

subject: Computer Networks
prompt: What does ARP resolve?
option_a: A domain name to an IP address
option_b: An IPv4 address to a MAC address
option_d: A MAC address to a domain name
explanation: ARP finds the link-layer address on the local network.

subject: Computer Networks
prompt: What is the order of the TCP three-way handshake?
explanation: The two sides exchange and acknowledge sequence numbers.

subject: Computer Networks
prompt: Which address is a private IPv4 address?
explanation: 192.168.0.0/16 is a private range under RFC 1918.

subject: Computer Networks
prompt: What is the main job of NAT?
option_b: Translating private addresses to a public address
explanation: NAT lets many private hosts share public addresses.

subject: Computer Networks
prompt: What can a layer 7 load balancer use to route requests?
option_d: The HTTP path or host header
explanation: Application-layer load balancers can inspect HTTP requests.

subject: Computer Networks
prompt: What does TLS provide for a typical HTTPS connection?
explanation: TLS protects data in transit and verifies the server certificate.
